newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom profits strong as rivals gather.
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom profits strong as rivals gather.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Telekom AG on Tuesday reported strong profits for 1996 and said earnings would more than double this year as the company girds for a full-scale assault on its home market by new competitors.

At its first results news conference since it launched Europe's largest ever share listing six months ago, Telekom set out to show that it was matching the ambitious forecasts made during months of road shows to woo investors.
While providing no comparative figure for the previous year, Telekom said group net profit was 1.8 billion marks ($1.1 billion) in 1996. Sales rose 6 percent to 63.1 billion marks ($37.1 billion).
Telekom Chairman Ron Sommer said he would defend Telekom's home market against new competitors and predicted its market share would not be eroded quickly.
"I expect the market development will remain moderate," he told the annual results news conference. "We will fight for every customer and we won't make it easy for our competitors."
